images.title: Three 60° angles make a line
images.purpose: Show why A, O and D lie on one straight line: the three 60° angles at O from OA round to OD add to 180°.
images.composition: One regular hexagon centred in the frame with a corner at the far left and the far right; the straight line AOD highlighted across it, white space around.
exact_structure: A regular hexagon with corners labelled A (far left), B (upper left), C (upper right), D (far right), E (lower right) and F (lower left), and centre labelled O.
Six thin dark segments from O to the six corners, making 6 equilateral triangles.
The three upper triangles AOB, BOC and COD filled alternately teal (#0072B2), amber (#E69F00), teal (#0072B2); the three lower triangles left white.
The straight line from A through O to D drawn thick in reddish purple (#CC79A7).
Three small angle arcs at O inside the upper triangles, each labelled 60°.
One short caption line under the hexagon.
rejection: any angle at O labelled other than 60°, or other than three 60° labels
other than 3 shaded upper triangles, or the hexagon not regular
A, O and D not on one straight line
images.takeaway: From OA round to OD is three 60° angles, which is 180°, so AOD is a straight line.
images.description: A regular hexagon split into six triangles, with the three upper triangles shaded, three 60° angles at O and the line AOD in reddish purple.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Count the three 60° wedges from A to D, then ask the same question for B, O, E and C, O, F.

image_decisions.why: The three wedges adding to a straight angle are much clearer seen than read.
